newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Mild earthquake rocks former Soviet Georgia.
newsitem.headline: Mild earthquake rocks former Soviet Georgia.

text.p: A earthquake measuring six on the Richter scale rocked the former Soviet republic of Georgia early on Monday, but regional officials said there were no reports of damage or casualties.
The state seismology service said the epicentre of the quake was in the remote Ninotsminda region, 80 km (50 miles) southwest of the capital Tbilisi, at 2:49 a.m. (2149 GMT).
Residents of Tbilisi said they felt two tremors about 30 minutes apart which rattled window panes.
The quake was felt as far away as Yerevan, capital of neighbouring Armenia.
A massive earthquake hit Armenia in 1988, killing thousands of people.
